sections.h2: Where is Monroeville, Pennsylvania, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
East of Pittsburgh in Allegheny County, Monroeville is a home rule municipality that counted 28,640 people in 2020. It covers about 19.7 square miles, and its elevation ranges from 735 to 1,319 feet, a spread of more than 580 feet from the lowest ground to the highest.

The municipality touches nine neighbors: Plum to the north, Murrysville, Penn Township and Trafford in Westmoreland County to the east and south, North Versailles, Wilmerding and Turtle Creek to the southwest, Wilkins Township to the west and Penn Hills to the northwest. The borough of Pitcairn sits entirely inside Monroeville, near the south-southwest edge, so check the parcel record to see which municipality's rules and tax rates apply to a given address.

sections.h2: How did Monroeville become a municipality?
sections.html:
The area takes its name from Joel Monroe, its first postmaster, and was settled in the mid to late 1800s. It was organized as Patton Township in 1849, became the borough of Monroeville on January 25, 1951, and adopted a Home Rule Charter on May 21, 1974.

Growth followed the highways and the retail boom. Population rose from 22,446 in 1960 to 29,011 in 1970 and 30,977 in 1980, then slipped to 28,386 by 2010 and 28,640 in 2020. The 2025 estimate of 27,685 is 3.3 percent under the 2020 base. That slow, flat pattern means most homes here belong to established neighborhoods rather than new subdivisions, and many were built in the decades when the population was climbing.

sections.h2: What drives Monroeville's economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Monroeville is best known for the Monroeville Mall, the surrounding office parks and a cluster of high-rise hotels that went up from the 1960s onward. The Monroeville Convention Center, once called the ExpoMart, sits near the mall. U.S. Steel's research laboratory here employed nearly 1,800 people at its 1979 peak.

The Census Bureau reports retail sales of about $2.59 billion in 2022, which works out to $91,813 per resident. That is far more than 27,000 residents spend alone, which shows how much shopping and service business Monroeville draws from the wider region. Health care and social assistance receipts were about $1.0 billion the same year.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and trails serve Monroeville homes?
sections.html:
Public school students from kindergarten through grade 12 attend the Gateway School District, which has about 3,800 students. Higher education nearby includes the Community College of Allegheny County's Boyce Campus, an Indiana University of Pennsylvania satellite site in Penn Center East and the Western School of Health and Business.

Getting around is straightforward:

  • Interstate 376, the Parkway East, carries traffic toward Pittsburgh and joins the Turnpike at Exit 57.
  • U.S. Route 22 is the main business route, with PA 48 and PA 286 serving other parts of the municipality.
  • Pittsburgh Regional Transit runs two bus lines to downtown from park-and-ride lots in Monroeville.
  • The Westmoreland Heritage Trail follows an old rail line to Trafford and Murrysville for cyclists and walkers.

Households here average only 2.20 people and 23.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, so plenty of Monroeville houses hold more space than their owners use. Owners without a mortgage pay a median of just $611 a month in housing costs, so a long-held home can be cheap to keep and still need expensive repairs.

sections.h2: Does Monroeville require an occupancy permit when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Yes. Monroeville requires a residential occupancy permit tied to the sale, and an inspection has to be completed before the new owners occupy the home. The municipality's application sets the fee at $100 for a single-family dwelling or townhome, and a second reinspection can add $50 under the municipal fee schedule.

The application works like this:

  • The current owner or the owner's agent files it.
  • It lists the property address, the buyer's name, who will meet the inspector and whether the electricity is on or off.
  • It has a line to mark the house as being sold as is.
  • The permit is issued in the name of the new owners who will live there.

The application lists 412-856-3340 for the municipality. Call before listing so the inspection can be scheduled early, and keep the electricity on if you can, since the form asks whether it is on or off.

sections.h2: What rules apply if the Monroeville house is a rental?
sections.html:
Rental units need their own occupancy permit, and an inspection must be completed before a tenant moves in. The fee is $75 for multi-family units and $100 for a single-family dwelling or townhome, and the permit is issued in the tenant's name. Units occupied before inspection can face penalty fines under the municipal ordinance.

A tenant in place changes the sale. Ask the municipality whether the permit on file is current and pass the paperwork to a buyer who plans to keep the tenant. An investor who will rent the house after closing applies under the rental rules separately from the sale permit. If the tenant is moving out anyway, put the move-out date in writing so the sale inspection can happen in an empty house.

sections.h2: What does a Monroeville sale cost in transfer tax, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
Monroeville is one of the higher-tax spots in the county table: 1 percent to the municipality and one-half percent to the Monroeville-Gateway school district, plus the state's 1 percent, for 2.5 percent in all. On a $210,000 sale that comes to $5,250. The tax goes to the county at the deeds office with its own check, apart from recording fees. Some family transfers escape it, and form REV-183 covers deeds that show no price.

A challenge to your valuation starts with BPAAR, the county's first appeal level, and all of its hearings take place by phone. You can speak for yourself, send an attorney or appoint a representative. A losing party may carry the case to the Board of Viewers in the Court of Common Pleas. The Gateway school district or the municipality can file an appeal against an owner too, and the owner is free to attend or skip those hearings.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Monroeville house quickly?
sections.html:
Speed depends on the inspection, the title and the buyer's financing. A cash buyer takes away the loan approval step, but the municipal occupancy inspection still applies.

  • Order the occupancy inspection early and fix any items it flags.
  • Pull the county parcel record for the owner of record and school district.
  • Collect mortgage and lien payoffs, and leave the power on for the inspector.
  • Weigh a listing, a cash offer and an as-is investor sale against what repairs would cost.

Monroeville sits where I-376, the Pennsylvania Turnpike at Exit 57, U.S. 22, Business 22 and PA 48 meet, and two Pittsburgh Regional Transit bus lines run to downtown Pittsburgh from park-and-ride lots here, so a listing can highlight the commute.

faqs.q: What is the occupancy permit fee when selling a house in Monroeville?
faqs.a: $100 for a single-family house or townhome under the municipal fee schedule, with a possible $50 charge if a second reinspection is needed. The buyers cannot occupy the home until the inspection is done.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Monroeville sale?
faqs.a: The county table gives 2.5 percent in all: the state takes 1 percent, the municipality 1 percent and the Monroeville-Gateway school district one-half percent.

faqs.q: Is Monroeville a city or a borough?
faqs.a: It is a home rule municipality. The area began as Patton Township in 1849, turned into a borough in 1951 and adopted its charter in 1974.
The Gateway School District serves students from kindergarten through grade 12. The Allegheny County transfer tax table lists it as the Monroeville-Gateway district for the municipality.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Monroeville property assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Go through the county's BPAAR board, which hears cases by phone. An owner may appear alone, use an attorney or name an authorized representative.
